conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi… I’ve been feeling really sick. Nauseous, throwing up, and my back pain’s been worse. My blood sugar’s been really high too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. When did the high blood sugars start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Two days ago. I wasn’t eating much because I felt off, but I kept taking my Lantus at night like usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And when did the vomiting start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yesterday. I couldn’t keep anything down, so I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Your blood sugar was 595 when you arrived, and we saw some ketones. That means you were in diabetic ketoacidosis. We gave you insulin and fluids in the ER to start correcting it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh… I didn’t realize it was that bad. I thought it was just another high sugar episode.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It was serious, but we’ve already started treatment. Your anion gap is closing, which means the acidosis is improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good… I hate feeling this way. It happens a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know this isn’t the first time. We’re going to keep you NPO for now—no food or drink by mouth—for the next few hours to let your stomach settle.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will I get something for the nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve given you Reglan and ondansetron through your IV. You should start feeling better soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. What about my back pain? It’s been really bothering me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your back—no tenderness. It might be related to your high sugars or muscle tension. We gave you dilaudid earlier, and we can continue with pain meds as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. I’ve had back pain since my car accident years ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see that in your history. You’re on gabapentin—still helping?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it helps some. I also use the lidocaine patch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep that up. We also did a CT scan of your abdomen and pelvis to make sure there’s nothing else going on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Was there anything wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The scan was clear—no abscess, no blockage. Your liver and pancreas look normal too. That’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried it might be my stomach again—like the gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know you’ve had that diagnosis, but your recent gastric emptying study was normal. Still, high sugars can make nausea worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I just don’t always know what triggers the highs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll work with the endocrinology team to adjust your insulin. They recommend lowering your Lantus dose to 24 units at bedtime.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: From 28? Why is that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because we want to avoid lows, especially since you’re not eating. We’ll also give you a tighter sliding scale for your Humalog.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I can follow that. I’ve messed up before by overcorrecting at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we saw that in your last admission. It’s important to balance correction without going too low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your blood sugar last night dropped to 230 and stayed in the 200s. This morning it’s 179—much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Can I eat something now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re going to start you on clear liquids and slowly advance to a regular diet. We’ll watch how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m really hungry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well with the clear liquids. We’re upgrading you to a regular diet for lunch.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. No nausea so far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your kidney function was a little off on admission—creatinine was 1.5—but it’s improving with fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from dehydration?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and possibly from your lisinopril. We held it temporarily, but we’ll restart it today since your levels are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I know I need to drink more water.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well. Your blood sugars are stable—no highs or lows—and you’ve kept your meals down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re discharging you today. We’ve updated your insulin: 24 units of glargine at bedtime and a new sliding scale for your aspart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll need to review the sheet carefully.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’ve also set up follow-up with your PCP, a counselor through social work, and GI for your esophageal varices.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve missed some appointments before… but I want to do better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a great step. Your team is here to support you. Keep using your nausea med as needed, and monitor your sugars closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for helping me through this again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call your doctor if you start feeling unwell again.
